# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 33 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_033_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 5, Chapter 1 — Patience and Anger

**1** "Be patient and long-suffering," he said, "and you will have mastery over all wickedness and will practice all righteousness. **2** For if you are patient, the Holy Spirit who dwells in you will remain pure, undarkened by any other evil spirit; he will dwell in a spacious place, rejoicing, and together with the vessel in which he dwells he will serve the Lord with great cheerfulness, having peace within himself. **3** But whenever an angry spirit enters, the Holy Spirit — being tender — immediately feels confined and has no clean place; he seeks to depart from it. For the angry spirit chokes him, leaving him no room to serve the Lord as he wishes, being defiled by the angry spirit. For the Lord dwells in patience, but the devil dwells in anger. **4** When both spirits inhabit the same place — when the one of anger enters — the Holy Spirit is grieved and that person is expelled from his presence. **5** The spirit of patience is dear to God and acceptable to him, and in patience the Lord dwells. The spirit of anger, however, is useless, and it destroys the person in whom it resides."

---

*LOGOS note: The description of the Holy Spirit as "tender" (hapalos) is theologically significant — the Spirit is not an irresistible force but a sensitive presence that can be displaced by contrary spiritual states. This is a relational pneumatology.*
